resiliaAI.title: ResiliaAI
resiliaAI.summary: An AI-powered resilience and crisis preparedness platform for housing associations and organizations.
resiliaAI.problem: A three-person venture needed one engineer to turn the product concept into a testable pre-launch platform.
built: The React and TypeScript product, APIs and PostgreSQL data layer.
Tests, continuous integration, delivery and hosted development environments.
proof: Sole engineer, from product decisions to implementation and release preparation.

maskera.title: Maskera
maskera.summary: Local redaction of Swedish personally identifiable information for browser, Node.js, edge, and AI workflows.
maskera.problem: Teams risk sending names, Swedish personal identity numbers and addresses to LLMs, logs and analytics.
built: Deterministic rules combined with a quantized ONNX model of about 43 MB.
Runs locally through Transformers.js with WebGPU or WASM.

proof.links: Live demo, npm package and Hugging Face model.

dataWipeMailer.title: Data Wipe Mailer
dataWipeMailer.summary: A privacy-focused web app that helps Swedish citizens send General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Article 17 deletion requests.
dataWipeMailer.problem: Getting removed from data brokers means finding each site's process and writing the same request over and over.
built: A client-side Next.js app that prepares a GDPR Article 17 request for each data broker.
Personal data stays in the browser and is never sent to a server.

proof.dfri: DFRI, the Swedish digital rights nonprofit, links to it in its privacy guide.
proof.redditEarlyFeedback: Reddit users tried it and called it useful. One got several automated replies within three minutes.
proof.redditIndependentShare: Another Reddit user shared it on their own as a reminder to clean up people-search sites.
proof.linkedin: LinkedIn launch post: 200,000+ views, 2,300+ reactions, 168 comments.

underStockholm.title: Under Stockholm
underStockholm.summary: The whole Stockholm metro in the browser: walk the platforms and ride the trains through all 100 stations.
underStockholm.problem: A metro you can explore in the browser has to feel like the real one, be shared between visitors and still load fast on a phone.
built: TypeScript, three.js and Rapier, no game engine.
Stations, textures and sounds are generated.
Trains follow a shared timetable or SL's live metro data.

proof.live: Playable at understockholm.com, source code public on GitHub.
proof.founderHouse: Presented live on stage at Claude Founder House Stockholm, Anthropic's event for 350+ founders and builders, in October 2026.
proof.feber: Covered by Feber, a Swedish tech news site, as a simulator where you ride along or drive the train.
proof.reddit: Reddit launch post in r/tunnelbana: 85,000+ views, 440+ upvotes, 60+ comments.
proof.linkedin: LinkedIn launch post: 15,000+ impressions, 280+ reactions, 30+ comments.

jarvisPanel.title: Jarvis Panel
jarvisPanel.summary: A 7-inch touch screen in my bookshelf with its own voice assistant. Say "Hey Jarvis" and it books the laundry room, adds events to my iCloud calendar and plays music, and at a glance it shows the metro, the weather and what is going on at home.
jarvisPanel.status: Runs at home daily · Open source
jarvisPanel.problem: I wanted a screen at home as fast as the one in a Tesla, that I can talk to, without a Big Tech speaker or trackers. My laundry room and gym booking sites have no open API.
built: Hardware: an off-the-shelf Waveshare ESP32-P4 7-inch touch board.
Firmware and UI: C++ with ESPHome and LVGL, with the wake word running locally on the screen.
Server: a Home Assistant integration and Python on a Raspberry Pi 5, where a Claude agent has tools for the calendar, the laundry room, SL, the weather and Spotify.
No ports open to the internet.
proof: Album cover at a track change: 3 s to under 0.15 s, measured on the screen.
AI agents flash every build and test it on the real hardware: they tap the screen over Wi-Fi, take screenshots and stop a build that got slower.
1,100+ automated tests run before every install.

jarvis.title: J.A.R.V.I.S
jarvis.summary: A private macOS assistant that connects local AI with personal notes, tools, and everyday workflows.
jarvis.problem: Personal notes and everyday tools live in separate apps. A cloud assistant would also expose private context.
jarvis.built: I built the app with SwiftUI, Ollama, and Model Context Protocol servers for iCloud Notes and Stockholm public transit.
jarvis.proof: The working macOS app reads notes and calls tools without cloud model dependencies.

torScraper.title: Tor Onion Site Scraper
torScraper.summary: A Python crawler and analysis pipeline developed for my bachelor thesis at Stockholm University.
torScraper.problem: The thesis needed repeatable data collection from cybercrime services hosted on Tor onion sites.
torScraper.built: I built a crawler that retrieves pages, extracts structured data, exports CSV files, and supports analysis with pandas and matplotlib.
torScraper.proof: Stockholm University published the thesis, and the crawler source code is public.
